outcomeStateAtFreeze.note: These interpretation and reporting rules are frozen before any independent second-annotation agreement result is recorded. They do not rewrite the original study plan or make the post-start addenda preregistered.

analysisBoundary.rule: All corpus results are descriptive of the checked-in historical reconstructions and supplied evidence sets. Do not generalize estimates to all ENS decisions, all grant programs, or institutional legitimacy.

constructValidity.improvementLimit: The current retrospective corpus has no untreated, alternative-workflow, or before/after comparator. It can describe reconstructability under the GDI ontology and expose ontology/tooling failure modes, but it cannot identify the comparative or causal effect implied by the study-plan word 'improve'.
constructValidity.burdenLimit: The current design has no predeclared burden comparator or proportionality threshold, and legacy primary elapsedMinutes values were not prospectively standardized. It can report bounded annotation-time observations but cannot establish that total administrative burden is proportionate or lower than an alternative process.
allowedConclusions: descriptive reconstructability and source-observability results for the sampled cases
descriptive ontology/model failure modes exposed by the sampled cases
descriptive annotation consistency for the independently double-annotated cases
bounded annotation-time observations under their stated measurement scopes
prohibitedConclusions: GDI improves reconstructability relative to an unspecified baseline
observed elapsedMinutes establishes institutional proportionality or adoption cost
the corpus demonstrates superiority to existing ENS decision-record practice
constructValidity.futureEvidenceNeeded: A comparative improvement or burden claim requires a prospectively specified comparator, outcome definition, measurement protocol, and analysis plan; where causal language is intended, the design must also justify causal identification.

primaryCorpusMetrics.rule: Retain the primary metrics declared in study-plan.json. Per-case values remain the direct analysis unit.

notAllowedAsConfirmatory: claims that aggregate summaries estimate all ENS decisions
aggregateReporting.note: Primary-annotation outcomes were already available when this addendum was created, so any newly added cross-case aggregate is explicitly post-hoc descriptive rather than preregistered primary analysis.

independentAnnotationAnalysis.selectedCaseRule: Use the three cases fixed by double-annotation-plan-2026-08-25.json. Do not replace a selected case because its agreement is low, high, inconvenient, or undefined.
independentAnnotationAnalysis.freezeRule: Compute agreement only from the two frozen independent annotations before reconciliation. Reconciled labels must never replace either pre-reconciliation annotation in reliability calculations.
cohenKappaRules: Report kappa as descriptive agreement evidence only.
If expected agreement equals 1, report kappa as undefined; do not substitute an arbitrary value.
Do not attach qualitative labels such as poor, fair, moderate, substantial, excellent, or near-perfect as if they were validated population categories.
Do not pool fields across cases into a single inferential kappa that treats nested field observations as independent population samples.

allowed: the three per-case raw agreements side by side
the three per-case kappas side by side when defined
macro-average raw agreement across the three selected cases, explicitly labeled descriptive
aggregate disagreement counts across the frozen field pairs, explicitly labeled descriptive
prohibitedClaims: reliability of all ENS decision records
annotation correctness or source truth inferred from agreement
statistical precision implied by the three-case minimum
crossCaseSummary.minimumInterpretation: Completing three selected cases satisfies the study-plan 25% double-annotation gate at the current corpus size, but three cases are insufficient for a strong population-level reliability claim.

primaryAnnotationTimes.rule: Previously recorded primary elapsedMinutes values may be reported as recorded metadata, but their operational scope was not prospectively standardized. Do not reinterpret them as complete administrative burden or directly comparable standardized task times.

secondAnnotationTimes.definition: Active time spent inspecting the supplied source set and producing the annotation submission, excluding unrelated breaks, communication, engineering/package preparation, and post-submission reconciliation.

prohibitedClaims: elapsedMinutes measures total institutional administrative burden
elapsedMinutes measures implementation or adoption cost
primary and second-annotation times are directly comparable unless their measurement scopes are demonstrated equivalent

reconciliationAnalysis.rule: Preserve every pre-reconciliation disagreement. Reconciliation may correct the case record or classify a disagreement, but must not alter the frozen reliability inputs.
report: record changes with preserved before/after hashes when applicable

missingAndUndefinedResults.rule: Unknown, not-applicable, unavailable evidence, and mathematically undefined agreement statistics are valid outcomes. Do not impute, drop, or relabel them to improve results.

finalReportRules: Identify the original study plan separately from every post-start addendum.
State the exact repository commit used to regenerate final metrics.
State explicitly that the present design does not identify an improvement effect or administrative-burden proportionality.
Report all three selected second-annotation cases, including unfavorable or undefined agreement results.
Separate preregistered primary metrics from post-hoc descriptive aggregates.
Separate legacy primary timing observations from prospectively standardized second-annotation timing.
Do not convert missing public evidence into evidence that a private process did not exist.
Do not convert validator success or inter-annotator agreement into substantive correctness, fairness, merit, or institutional legitimacy.
nonClaims: This addendum is not part of the original preregistration.
This addendum does not erase that primary-annotation outcomes were already known when it was written.
Freezing second-annotation interpretation rules before agreement outcomes reduces outcome-contingent analysis flexibility but does not make the corpus statistically representative.
No independent second annotation is created or implied by this file.
